Review for The Operator on Steam

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ (5/5)

The Operator is a standout tactical shooter that excels in every aspect. The game combines deep strategy with gripping storytelling, offering a rewarding experience from start to finish. The mission design is superb, the graphics are stunning, and the real-time command system adds layers of tactical depth. The narrative is engaging, with excellent voice acting and a compelling plot that keeps you hooked. With high replay value and ongoing updates, this game is a must-play for fans of the genre. Highly recommended!

First things first - the game needs a sequel! May that serve as a testament to how fun this particular title is. The entire game is you exploring the narrative of the story through the interface of your computer terminal at the FDI, supporting field agents in their investigations. Analysing evidence, using various tools to ascertain information and ultimately being drawn into a conspiracy with quite the twist at the end of it -hence the need for a sequel. If you are looking for a chill, relaxing romp of a story you can't go wrong with this one.

This is definitely one of the games of all time. An experience. Immersive, poignant story with a deep lore for a 3-4 hours playthrough. Music is awesome and fitting. A solid 9/10. Only wish it was longer.

The Operator was so unique and so fun, and genuinely floored me several times. There's a handful of story pieces that maybe I'd do differently, but nothing that would deter me from the game or from recommending it. Puzzles are challenging without feeling impossible, and somehow I felt affection for some of the characters. Wish the POV character was voice acted, but otherwise I absolutely loved this game

What an amazing experience this game is.
A well written story with excellent pacing, and also very good voice acting. It features amazing sound design that really cements the suspense and excitement that this game portrays so well.

The gameplay is simplistic, but shows a lot of thought and care in its design.
You play with a virtual tabletop where you'll navigate files, folders and the chat-system you utilise to communicate with agents. You'll be scanning pictures and videos for details, and cross-check data with the company database that lists any person you can identify with a full name or via face recognition, among other things...

As I finished the game I was filled with a hunger for more. And the systems implemented in this game leaves nigh limitless potential for future projects based on the same concept. I loved every second playing this game, and I hope to see more from this developer in the future.
Exceeded my expectations. Very immersive, interesting story, fun puzzle-solving. Joj (don't worry about it) thought it was great too

[b]TIPS[/b]: [i]If you buy this game and you get up to the third day of work on Wells Case list, I highly recommend that when you get to the evidence room to uncensor those classified documents you also uncensor KAndrews case's summary by reverting it back to the old version. Just as an extra![/i]

A lot about The Operator is fantastic. Major kudos to writers & sound designers. Lot of inspiration & very clever ideas. I've spent some memorable evenings with this game.

AND YET I have been hesitant to recommending it, as the narrative will feel, to many, thoroughly unsatisfying. More about this below, under spoiler tags.

But all in all, barring that, the game's solid, and I did have a lot of fun with it. It simply did not take me where I wanted to go.

[spoiler]The ending is terrible. It betrays the player in a way that was absolutely not needed, clumsily trying to set up expectations for a sequel while, because of its violence & disregard for the player, destroying any desire for one. I know I said above that the writing was solid, EXCEPT for this part: what were you thinking? What was the point of making me do all of this if that's what do you do in the end? That's a major disappointment. Don't bother continuing this story, create something new - and learn from your mistakes. [/spoiler]

First and foremost, I really enjoyed the characters, dialogue, puzzles, and story. I saw many comments saying that the twist was unexpected and, after having played the game myself, I'm going to have to agree that I ALSO did not see that coming! 

I feel it is worth mentioning that, one of the more unforgiving elements of this game is that you are unable to save and restart at the beginning of a chapter/day. Therefore, if you miss an achievement, you have to start the game all over again. This brings me to the next unforgiving aspect of this game which is that no dialogue or cut scene is skippable or able to be fast-forwarded (e.g. clicking to make dialogue scroll faster). 

Despite the fact that these elements made the game a little more frustrating, I welcome the challenge. It doesn't take away from my positive review nor my recommendation for others to check this game out. If anything, it makes the achievements feel earned. Additionally, the game is not very long. So, a few restarts shouldn't lock the player into an unrelenting commitment of innumerable hours. I put just 6.5 hours into the game and, to put my point into perspective, I restarted the game twice -- to get all 13 achievements.

GREAT Experience!! Despite its relatively short length, The Operator left me thoroughly engrossed in every minute of gameplay. The intuitive puzzles, combined with the engaging narrative, make it a standout title in the genre. My only complaint is that I was left wanting more by the end of it.

If you’re a fan of narrative-driven games and enjoy solving intricate puzzles, I highly recommend giving “The Operator” a try. It’s a game that tests your detective skills and keeps you on the edge of your seat from start to finish.

If you are looking for a good puzzle/detective guy in the chair game to scratch that itch made by an indie developer to entertain you for 3 hours with great gameplay, great puzzles that don't hold your hand and are satisfying to solve, great voice acting, introducing a couple of interesting game mechanics beyond "click face and search for name here" and a pretty good linear story, then this is the game for you. I bought it at 10% off and really enjoyed it, will definitely be on the look out for the next game this developer makes, and would recommend it to anyone with the expectation that its a good indie game.  

If you are looking for a deep, multi ending detective game where choices matter and there's endless replayability, this is not the game for you. I think the two critiques I see the most of is that fact the game is short and doesn't have multiple endings. For the length side, I think complaining that a game isn't long enough is a pretty good complaint to have. The game isn't perfect, but its entertaining and I hope the developer makes a longer game in the future using the success from this game to better utilize some of the interesting game mechanics that get introduced but then not used again (there's a few). 

Whether it's worth the price is subjective. The developer gave the reasoning that it's about the length of a movie, around the price of similar games, and so that's why it's at the price that it is. I don't know how much that justifies the price for this game, which I feel is a few dollars more expensive than similar games, but since I liked the demo, the movie comparison seemed reasonable enough for me (at least given some reason instead of no reason at all) and I wanted to support the developer, so I went for it when it first released. Overall, I am very satisfied with the game, had a good time, and would buy it again. 

Not having multiple endings doesn't bother me much. If the "choices" are scattered throughout the game, I'm not replaying, solving puzzles I already know the answers too, just to change a couple of dialogue options. The same thing for if the choice is at the end and there's no individual save feature for me to go back to. I think it's fair to expect an indie developer to just make a game that's fun to play once. There's dialogue options that don't really matter, but I found the characters you interact with the most really endearing and felt connected very quickly.

I'm [i]really[/i] glad to have a game like this where the story isn't just "surveillance bad".

The mechanics are good though sometimes it can be hard to scan things even when you know what to scan. Special ways to solve problems are generally only used once and can be decently complex and fun because of that. They're usually a refreshing change and can be [i]incredibly[/i] intense. I just wish certain things would be randomized between attempts.

Now for the story. Like I said, I'm very glad it didn't go for the usual story this type of game attracts. It's a fairly decent plot with likeable, well voiceacted characters and let's you figure out certain things early without being utterly obvious.

The problem is the ending. The rest will be in spoilers, though I'm not gonna say anything specific. This is basically just for people that are really adverse to any kind spoiler, no matter how small.

[spoiler]The story is very good at making you think that your choices matter; though they ultimate do not. The stakes feel astronomical in multiple situations, but turn out to be utterly meaningless in the end. And there's no easy way to say this, but:

The ending sucks. Ruining the rest of the game levels of bad.

For starters, there is only one, even if it might seem you'd have at least 2 paths to go down. On top of that it is abrupt, doesn't make any sense and the person responsible for said ending was probably meant to seem really intimidating and constantly in control. This is not the case and the person ends up looking incredibly incompetent and only seems to succeed because everyone else is even more of an idiot.

I can not overstate enough that the entire game was fun - only for the entire mood to be ruined at the end, seemingly just to set up a sequel that could've easily focused on a different conspiracy. I genuinely do not know how it was fumbled this badly.[/spoiler]

"The Operator" is an incredibly enjoyable experience that draws you deep into the world of digital investigation and conspiracy. As an operator for the FDI, I found myself thoroughly engrossed in solving complex cases, and the game kept me on the edge of my seat from start to finish.

Pros:

Engaging Mechanics: The investigative tools are a highlight of the game. Analyzing evidence, digging through databases, and assisting field agents in real-time was so satisfying that I often wished I had more time to use these tools.

Gripping Narrative: Each case is a well-crafted story with twists and turns that kept me hooked. Although I figured out the major twist halfway through, it was set up nicely and added to the overall tension rather than detracting from it.

Atmospheric Tension: The game excels at creating a sense of paranoia and urgency. The mysterious presence of the cyber criminal HAL and the cryptic messages to "trust no one" added layers of psychological depth that kept me fully engaged. There's one part of the game that had me sweating buckets because it was so tense, but I won’t spoil anything—just be prepared!

Cons:

Not Enough Time with the Tools: My only real gripe is that the game could have given us more opportunities to dive deeper into the mechanics. The tools are so well-designed that I wanted to spend even more time exploring their capabilities.

A Bit Short: The game is on the shorter side, but considering it was developed by a very small team (possibly just one or two people), what they’ve created is nothing short of incredible. I sincerely hope to see more from them in the future.

Anyone who appreciates immersive narratives and detective games should definitely play this one. The game provides an exciting experience with tough puzzles and a gripping narrative that will keep you wondering. Although some may find the twist predictable, it's skillfully done and doesn't take away from the overall experience. Even with its length, it's an amazing accomplishment for such a small team, and I can't wait to see what they come up with next.

Unfortunate to release a game like this in-between the Golden Idol game, as it makes look like it could a smilar type of investigation game. This is not really the case, even though you could really batch it with it and Obra Dinn as point & click made for people prejudicied against point & click, The Operator have more stronger emphasis on its narrative over the actual case solving.

This probably no biggest departure between what you could expect compared to what the game delivers so it's probably what needs to be the clearest : this isn't some X-files case solving about solving stranges cases and chasing aliens, this is short narrative game. While I kinda wish it had more filler cases, that would require to use all the different tools to solve, it's clearly outside the scope of this game. The story itself is a very typical thriller, to the point is possible to get where it's trying to go just because the trope used are that common and maybe it would a problem if this was a visual novel.

The obvious gimmick here is the entire game is told through the screen of a computer, a very limited dispositive that get the most out of the very conventional plot. This may sound dismissive thriller are very codified type of story, that's part of the interest in even saying "this is a thriller", the same way I expect to see a group of young people sharing their sob stories and their way to save the world in my J-RPG. So how do you make something like this interesting when you can't hire Keanu Reeves to do cool stuff on screen ? What the Operator does is giving as little as possible. Low quality camera footage, damaged photography, unreliable testimony, chat windows and a lot of phone calls, an quick acces to a lot clues but very little interaction with the actual narrative. Backed-up by the dynamic soundtrack, this game creates some pretty sincere moment of tension. Especially when the main character position matches the player playing the game, good for immersion even if you don't emphasize too much with the character (I didn't really, sorry).

I do think this game overall is a bit short and lack a bit of substance as an investigation game, but is a narrative game really dedicated to its theme.

First, let me just say, the cinematics in The Operator are the most awful extended cinematics I've EVER seen. They'll appear between the days, after you finish work. They consist of blurry lights and shades of movement (nothing is in focus) followed by irritating audio, like swallowing, gulping, walking, groaning, animal noises and so on. You better pay attention and listen to these because they're actually important to the story and needed to solve some puzzles. While watching and listening to these CINEMATICS, I've never felt more inclined to take my monitor and throw it out the window in a fit of pure rage. Are these meant to induce anger? The designer of these visually deprived cinematics is an obvious super-fan of ASMR.

Apart from that, yeah it's good. Good story, twists, neat puzzles and the characters are interesting. The story doesn't take any more of your time than it needs to and, yeah, was overall pretty good. A bit too paranoid for me but, you know, still good.

A 1990's-era X-Files-inspired game, you play as the titular Operator, one of many multi-talented personell tasked with assisting the agents of the Federal Department of Investigation (FDI), the fictional counterpart to the US FBI and, eventually, uncover a strange conspiracy.

The voice acting is excellent, really bringing life to all the characters. The puzzles are all logical and clever, especially if you keep track of prior cases.

The story is also excellent. It's only ~2 hours long, but it feels much longer than that, not because of padding, but because it manages to pack in a lot of meaningful intrigue and story beats in those 2 hours. It also has some excellent twists.

Would definitely recommend!

The game kind of struggles with what it actually wants you to do and who it wants you to be.

To get started: I really wanted to love this game, because I like researching and playing detective. However you are given a set of tools and expectations to be resourceful, while actually non of it works outside the main storyline. 

As a package it is nicely crafted and for a while it has you engaged, but at some points it expects you to really take control and go beyond the objective ... but only in the exact path the developer(s) have set out for you. The developer(s) haven't realized that it becomes very frustrating, very fast that the game doesn't allow you to explore or make combinations other than that what they exactly have programmed you to do. So encouraging you to think beyond one case, but at the same time limiting your possibilities very much gets your frustrated easily. Sure there is a subpath that you miss sometimes, but you only miss it because all your other attempts to try something different aren't supported (like you can't call anyone on your own or analyse something that isn't supposed to be analyzed). If you don't have any room to play / experiment, you stop doing it and than at some point the game will make fun of you and point out that you have missed something.

Same goes for the dialogs. The game keeps asking you to select an answer while none of it really matters, it is all linear! Again it learns you to make choices, but the choices don't matter so why are they even there than? Just for a single different line of text to go back to the main story path again?

I'll try to give it a go some more when I am less frustrated. But for now, it has got me fed up.
